walkthroughs.body_html:
The Challenge of Resource Management — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Challenge of Resource Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Challenge of Resource Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the Hubbert curve about?
options: Peak oil
Population
Climate
Migration
Africa
South America
Australia
Central Asia

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
